### M4-E02 · Fernanda's books, now in one line

> **SOURCE · question posed in the lecture**  
> Source: [lecture4 L280-304](../../sources/lecture4.txt) *“SELECT title FROM longlist WHERE the name equals Fernanda.”*

| Topic / concepts | Difficulty | Skills | Dataset | Task type |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C4.2 | ★ | querying a view | `longlist` | write a query |

The `longlist` view exists. Using **only the view**, return the titles Fernanda Melchor wrote.
Compare this with your three-level subquery from M1-E08.

<details><summary>Setup the checker runs first</summary>

```sql
CREATE VIEW "longlist" AS
SELECT "name", "title" FROM "authors"
JOIN "authored" ON "authors"."id" = "authored"."author_id"
JOIN "books" ON "books"."id" = "authored"."book_id";
```
</details>

<details><summary>Expected output (try first!)</summary>

| title |
|---|
| Paradais |
| Hurricane Season |

</details>

### M4-E04 · A temporary view built on a view

> **SOURCE · demonstrated in the lecture**  
> Source: [lecture4 L588-612](../../sources/lecture4.txt) *“I'll say create a temporary view.”*

| Topic / concepts | Difficulty | Skills | Dataset | Task type |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C4.3, C4.4 | ★★ | CREATE TEMPORARY VIEW, view on view | `longlist` | change the database |

Using `average_book_ratings`, create a **temporary** view `average_ratings_by_year` with columns
`year` and `rating` (the average of the books' averages for that year, rounded to 2 decimals).

<details><summary>Setup the checker runs first</summary>

```sql
CREATE VIEW "average_book_ratings" AS
SELECT "book_id", "title", "year", ROUND(AVG("rating"), 2) AS "rating"
FROM "ratings" JOIN "books" ON "ratings"."book_id" = "books"."id"
GROUP BY "book_id";
```
</details>

<details><summary>Expected output (try first!)</summary>

After your SQL, the checker runs:

`SELECT * FROM "average_ratings_by_year"`

| year | rating |
|---|---|
| 2018 | 3.75 |
| 2019 | 3.64 |
| 2020 | 3.93 |
| 2021 | 3.69 |
| 2022 | 3.87 |
| 2023 | 3.78 |

`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_temp_master WHERE "name" = 'average_ratings_by_year'`

| COUNT(*) |
|---|
| 1 |

</details>

### M4-E13 · Assigned: INSTEAD OF INSERT for genuinely new items

> **SOURCE · explicitly left to the learner in the lecture**  
> Source: [lecture4 L1331-1336](../../sources/lecture4.txt) *“For now though, we leave all that up to you.”*, [lecture4 L1236-1242](../../sources/lecture4.txt) *“In that case, actually inserting a brand new row”*

| Topic / concepts | Difficulty | Skills | Dataset | Task type |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C4.8 | ★★★★ | INSTEAD OF trigger, WHEN NOT IN | `mfa` | change the database |

The lecture ends: *"I could write a trigger to actually add a brand new row to this table here … we leave all that up to you."*
Write `"insert_when_new"`: when the inserted accession number does **not** exist yet, insert a real new row into `collections`.
The checker inserts one brand-new artwork and one re-acquired artwork.

<details><summary>Setup the checker runs first</summary>

```sql
ALTER TABLE "collections" ADD COLUMN "deleted" INTEGER DEFAULT 0;
UPDATE "collections" SET "deleted" = 1 WHERE "title" = 'Imaginative Landscape';
CREATE VIEW "current_collections" AS
SELECT "id", "title", "accession_number", "acquired" FROM "collections" WHERE "deleted" = 0;
CREATE TRIGGER "insert_when_exists" INSTEAD OF INSERT ON "current_collections" FOR EACH ROW
WHEN NEW."accession_number" IN (SELECT "accession_number" FROM "collections")
BEGIN
    UPDATE "collections" SET "deleted" = 0 WHERE "accession_number" = NEW."accession_number";
END;
```
</details>

<details><summary>Expected output (try first!)</summary>

After your SQL, the checker runs:

`SELECT "title", "accession_number", "deleted" FROM "collections"`

| title | accession_number | deleted |
|---|---|---|
| Farmers Working at Dawn | 11.6152 | 0 |
| Imaginative Landscape | 56.496 | 1 |
| Profusion of Flowers | 56.257 | 0 |
| Spring Outing | 14.76 | 0 |

</details>
